item.title: 2170 Assembly-Line Good Yield: About 40%→98.7%
item.description:
Problem and context

Good-product yield on the 2170 assembly line was initially about 40%. Before increasing output, we had to distinguish whether losses came from the product, equipment, or inspection. Treating a gauge error as a process defect can lead to the wrong process change; treating a real defect as an inspection issue allows it to recur.

I therefore started by aligning production quantity, inspected quantity, defect categories, downtime, and measurement rules rather than tuning one recipe from a headline yield number.

item.title: Evidence- and Rights-Governed Maintenance Learning: Why PUBLIC and HOLD Both Matter
item.description:
Problem: a fluent explanation is not necessarily a supported answer

Qualification material fragments questions, answers, theory, NCS units, and practical visuals across sources. AI can fill gaps fluently while still relying on:

  • conflicting answer candidates;
  • images without publication rights;
  • theory that is textually similar but semantically wrong;
  • answers already present in a pre-submit client payload;
  • one UI forced across written and practical answer formats.

The project goal is therefore not rapid question growth. It is a platform that publishes only evidence-qualified learning and preserves uncertainty as HOLD.

item.title: Fail-Closed AI Authority & Evidence Plane: Visibility Is Not Execution Authority
item.description:
Problem: test success is not execution authority

These statements describe different facts:

  • a model read data;
  • a model recommended an action;
  • local code passed tests;
  • an authorized person approved a bounded action;
  • the same artifact ran in the operating environment;
  • an external effect occurred and was read back.

Without that separation, “test PASS” can become “ready to deploy,” recommendation can become order approval, and local state can be mistaken for external effect.

item.title: NCM Prismatic Pilot Line: FAT/SAT for 13 Processes and 11 Systems
item.description:
Problem and context

An automatic cycle on one machine does not mean a pilot line is ready. Upstream and downstream interfaces, cycle time, precision, repeatability, sensors, alarms, interlocks, operator safety, and recovery must work together. After product input, measurement variation must also be separated from process variation.

This project covered 13 detailed processes and 11 core systems on an NCM 50Ah prismatic-cell assembly pilot line.

What I owned

  • Prepared FAT/SAT acceptance sheets and checked specifications, intermediate-part tolerances, and acceptance criteria.
  • Managed vendor punch lists, action dates, and retest results.
  • Reviewed process capability (Cpk) separately from the measurement system (Gage R&R).
  • Checked laser, ultrasonic, and resistance welding plus filling through tensile, cross-section, leak, Hi-Pot, IR, and X-ray results.
  • Managed materials, WIP, staffing, and lot history for a 200-cell daily plan.
  • Used and improved an Excel VBA tracking sheet where MES was not yet available.

What I checked and changed

Stage Checks Method
FAT Function, cycle, I/O, alarms, interlocks, safety Specification and acceptance-sheet comparison; punch registration
Installation Utilities, reference points, precision, repeatability Recheck after installation
SAT Interfaces, sample run, restart, and recovery Repeated tests under site conditions
Process check Cpk, Gage R&R, welding, and filling Compared process and measurement variation separately
Production operation Material, WIP, people, lots, daily output Managed priorities against the 200-cell plan

Process capability (Cpk) describes the stability of process output against specification. Gage R&R checks variation from the measurement system and operators. They are not one “process index.”

item.title: Official-source Unemployment Benefit Q&A: Turning 165 Questions into Verification Paths
item.description:
Problem: similar questions can produce different administrative outcomes

A short question such as “Can I qualify after resigning?” may depend on separation reason, insured periods, documents, job-search activity, an individual notice, and agency review. A website that decides the case can conflict with current law or the actual disposition.

The service is therefore a static verification aid, not an eligibility chatbot. It helps a user find:

  • the closest question type;
  • facts and documents to check;
  • the relevant Work24, ministry, or statute source;
  • what to confirm through an individual notice or competent employment center.

Why 165 questions become eight categories

Publishing raw conversations would expose personal context and create duplicates. One giant FAQ would make discovery difficult.

item.title: Semiconductor and Display-Part Surface Treatment and Measurement Correlation
item.description:
Problem and context

Surface-treatment results change with material, geometry, contamination, and process conditions even when a nominal recipe is unchanged. My scope included chemical anodizing, etching, and cleaning as well as dry mechanical bead blasting. Because those processes work differently, I managed their conditions and inspection methods separately instead of grouping all of them as wet processing. Even stable internal measurements can fail qualification when the customer’s instrument and rule differ.

item.title: Vacuum-Robot Overhaul: Turning Verbal Know-How into SOPs
item.description:
Problem and context

Vacuum-robot overhaul does not end with cleaning and parts replacement. Arm alignment, encoder zero, vacuum leak, and repeatability must be within the acceptance rule before the robot returns to equipment. Work order and inspection know-how had depended heavily on individual experience, leading to different assembly times and missed checks.

What I owned

  • Performed disassembly, cleaning, and bearing, belt, and motor replacement.
  • Checked arm alignment, encoder zero, vacuum leak, repeatability, teaching, and commissioning.
  • Documented parts lists, disassembly/assembly order, torque, alignment, and inspection criteria.
  • Trained operators with SOPs and checklists and reviewed their first work.
  • Supported overseas line setup and sample overhaul; the public result stops at the initial sample qualification I directly confirmed during employment.

What I checked and changed

Stage Checks Documented baseline
Incoming/disassembly External condition, motion, part locations Incoming checklist and disassembly order
Cleaning/replacement Contamination, bearings, belts, motors Replacement criteria and parts list
Assembly Fastening order, torque, arm position Assembly sequence and cautions
Alignment/zero Arm alignment and encoder zero Reference and check method
Final inspection Leak, repeatability, teaching, commissioning Test order, decision, and abnormal-response steps

The documents were written so the next operator could follow the same assembly order and find an abnormality through the same tests.

item.title: Deep Learning Modeling Textbook: Reproducible Experiments for Manufacturing Data
item.description:
Problem: executable training code is not yet a reproducible experiment

Deep Learning Modeling Textbook is a personal learning and practical validation project for organizing data preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and reproducibility as one traceable workflow. Instead of stopping at isolated tutorial code, the project defines a modeling standard that can be reused when new data arrives: frame the problem, run a controlled experiment, and explain the result.

The public repository currently exposes only limited implementation detail. This case study is therefore a design document based on the repository’s stated scope of preprocessing, training, evaluation, and reproducibility management. It does not claim a particular dataset size, model accuracy, completed training run, or production deployment. The directory structure and validation items below are target design criteria, not a list of finished features.

item.title: AI Welding Vision: Designing Metrics Around Missed-Defect Risk
item.description:
Problem: accuracy alone cannot define a welding-defect operating threshold

Item Verified scope
Problem Micro-defect features overlapped with normal surfaces, data was imbalanced, and accuracy alone did not represent the cost of passing a defective weld.
Role I was responsible for evaluation-metric design and validation, including F1, recall, false-positive behavior, and threshold interpretation.
Action The team separated roughly 60,000 AI-Hub images from 198 field images, compared a DenseNet baseline, a two-model combination, and a ResNet+DeiT ensemble, then reviewed a second test set and tuned the decision threshold to prioritize missed-defect control.
Result On the recorded evaluation set and selected threshold, the report lists F1 93.10%, Recall 100%, and Precision 87.07%. These values do not establish production-wide generalization.
Evidence The public report’s dataset, model-evolution, second-test, threshold, and final-metric slides; no dedicated public repository.

Resume bullets

  • Separated approximately 60,000 public welding images and 198 field images by learning/field-validation purpose instead of presenting them as one undifferentiated training set.
  • Compared DenseNet, a two-model combination, and a ResNet+DeiT ensemble, then used second-test error review to tune the operating threshold around missed-defect cost.
  • Recorded F1 93.10%, Recall 100%, and Precision 87.07% on the stated evaluation set and defined manual reinspection as the control for remaining false positives.

Interview STAR

  • Situation: Missing a small weld defect carried a higher quality risk than sending a normal part to reinspection, while accuracy could remain high under class imbalance.
  • Task: Establish a comparable evaluation framework and a decision threshold aligned with that asymmetric risk.
  • Action: Separate data sources, compare model stages on the same metrics, inspect mixed normal/defect regions in a second test, and search thresholds that retained recall.
  • Result: The selected evaluation produced Recall 100%, F1 93.10%, and Precision 87.07%. I also documented that this is inspection-assistance evidence, not proof of autonomous production deployment.

Why this project was structured this way

item.title: Collaborative-Robot Assembly Twin and Edge-Vision PoC
item.description:
The problem

Separate demonstrations of robot motion, vision results, PLC sequences, and MES records do not reconstruct what happened to one product.

This education team PoC used a QR serial as the common key across an Indy7 assembly flow, edge-vision inspection, PLC and SCADA, MySQL/MES, and digital-twin state.

Area Public scope
Project type Education team PoC
My role Robot and Digital Twin
Team implementation QR traceability, robot sequence, vision, PLC/SCADA, and MES
Technologies Indy7, Python, YOLO, Raspberry Pi, Hailo, PLC, and MySQL
Current status Education demo complete; plant pilot and long-running E2E unverified

Team output and my individual role are kept separate. I do not present the full team result as a solo achievement, and the original report containing teammate identities is not published.

item.title: Giga Press Factory DX: From Field Signals to Virtual Commissioning
item.description:
Problem: process and communication risk must be tested before equipment deployment

Item Verified scope
Problem Process sequences and parameter assumptions could only be checked late with physical equipment, while PLC, SCADA, and virtual-model data integrity was hard to review in advance.
Role In a ten-person team, I worked in the Digital Twin group on AI-model selection/training, communications setup, and technical research. Ladder and SCADA implementation belonged to other team members and is not presented as my individual work.
Action I mapped the Factory I/O–PLC–SCADA–OPC UA data path, reviewed the DQN control candidate, and defined the boundary between control, monitoring, and AI-assisted optimization.
Result The team integrated process flow, Ladder/Factory I/O, SCADA, web, and AI-extension concepts into one demonstration and report. The cited 50–75% setup reduction and 50% expansion-labor reduction are expected benefits/targets, not measured factory outcomes.
Evidence The team report’s R&R table, architecture, result, and expected-benefit slides; no dedicated public source repository.

Resume bullets

  • Owned AI-model selection/training and OPC UA communications scope in a ten-person manufacturing-DX project that connected Factory I/O, PLC, SCADA, and a virtual commissioning scenario.
  • Converted battery-line FAT/SAT experience into failure-oriented checks covering missing sensors, communication delay, restart conditions, and safe PLC authority.
  • Kept the report’s 50–75% setup and 50% expansion-effort figures as pre-production targets rather than presenting them as measured plant savings.

Interview STAR

  • Situation: High-capital equipment creates late discovery risk because control logic and data integrity are difficult to test before physical trial.
  • Task: My scope was to define where AI and communications fit so that control and monitoring layers used consistent data without giving AI unrestricted equipment authority.
  • Action: I organized the OPC UA data flow, reviewed DQN as an optimization candidate, and kept deterministic control and safety checks inside the PLC boundary.
  • Result: The team produced an integrated simulation and report. Quantified values remained expected benefits until controlled before/after measurement is available.

item.title: HeungTology: Finding Industrial Knowledge with Traceable Sources
item.description:
The problem

Manufacturing knowledge is split across process, equipment, quality, defect, and corrective-action documents. As the collection grows, one machine acquires several names, relationships point to missing records, and unsupported explanations enter search results.

HeungTology is not a document-count project. It is a personal project for validating human-edited documents, tracing process and equipment relationships, and showing which source section supports a retrieved answer.

Area Public scope
Problem Duplicate identities, broken relationships, weak provenance, and local-path leakage
My scope Data structure, transformation and validation, graph representation, and retrieval design
Technologies YAML, JSON Schema, JSON-LD, OWL, SHACL, Neo4j, and Python
Current status Described only within the code and documentation visible in the public repository
Withheld claims Local release counts and completion ratings that cannot be reproduced from a public report

Why it is structured this way

Keeping authoring, graph exchange, and retrieval data in one hand-maintained file makes drift likely. The project therefore separates their responsibilities.

item.title: Indy7 JSON, PC-HMI, and Digital-Twin Design
item.description:
The problem

A robot program is more than a list of joint positions. Tool and TCP settings, waypoints, motion commands, branches, speed, and I/O fields reference one another. If a PC editor reads only familiar fields and rewrites the file, the result may look correct on screen while failing on the teach pendant.

Communication has a similar ownership problem. If the HMI, historian, and digital twin each open a robot socket, it becomes difficult to identify the command owner and the latest state.

item.title: resumOpenAI: An Evidence-aware Resume Generation PoC
item.description:
Problem: controlling career facts matters more than fluent generation

resumOpenAI explores a narrower problem than “ask an LLM to write a resume.” It separates verified career facts, private fields, target-role selection, draft generation, and output validation so that polished wording cannot silently alter dates, employers, roles, or measured outcomes.

Area Design
Frontend React form and draft review
API Flask request validation and generation orchestration
Data structured career facts with evidence/status fields
LLM controlled prompt and optional adaptation path
Safety personal-data minimization and public/private separation
QA claim/date/number checks before export

Why structure comes before fine-tuning

Fine-tuning can make style more consistent, but it cannot repair missing or contradictory facts. The first quality gate is a structured source model.
